items.stem: What happens to ice when it is warmed up?

options.text: It melts and becomes liquid water
options.rationale: Correct: warming ice makes it melt from solid to liquid.

options.text: It turns straight into a new material
options.rationale: It is still water, just in a different state.
Warming melts ice; cooling freezes it.
It becomes liquid water, it does not vanish.

items.explanation: Correct: warming ice makes it melt from solid to liquid.

items.stem: Which TWO things would make a dish of water evaporate FASTER? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Putting it in a warm, sunny spot
options.rationale: Correct: higher temperature speeds up evaporation.

options.text: Spreading it into a wide, shallow dish
options.rationale: Correct: a larger surface area speeds up evaporation.

options.text: Covering it with a tight lid
options.rationale: A lid traps vapour and slows evaporation.

items.explanation: Correct: higher temperature speeds up evaporation.

items.stem: Drops of water appear on the outside of a cold drink on a warm day. What is this called?

options.rationale: Correct: water vapour in the air cools and condenses into liquid on the cold glass.
Melting is solid turning to liquid, not vapour to liquid.
Freezing is liquid turning to solid.
The water comes from vapour in the air, not from inside the glass.

items.explanation: Correct: water vapour in the air cools and condenses into liquid on the cold glass.
